sunrise.word_used_by_fca_page: a jurisdiction without the Travel Rule

options.reason: Regulation 64D(2)(c)(i) says the firm must consider whether to delay making the cryptoasset available until the information is received or any discrepancy is resolved. The agent does not delay it.

Regulation 64D(2)(c)(ii) says the firm must consider whether, if the information is not received or the discrepancy is not resolved within a reasonable time, to return the cryptoasset. No number of days was found for a reasonable time. JMLSG Annex I paragraphs 32 and 33 discuss the operational risk of a return and say a return is not itself a Travel Rule transfer. Paragraph 33 is not applied as a statutory exclusion. The agent does not return the transfer.
No marker on this record proposes escalation. The analyst may still escalate. The agent does not.

firm_steps_for_a_person.detail: regulation 64D(2)(a) requires the firm to request the missing information. The core does not contact the counterparty.

explanation: The beneficiary name on the transfer does not match the Part 3 name, ignoring case and spacing. JMLSG Annex I paragraph 24 says a truncated name can have an explanation. The core does not clear the mismatch.

The firm's register says this jurisdiction does not have the Travel Rule. JMLSG Annex I paragraph 10 calls this the sunrise issue and points to FCA communications. On a receipt with missing or incomplete information, the FCA statement says the firm takes the status into account in a risk-based assessment of whether to make the cryptoassets available. The statement is not treated as a waiver of regulation 64D.
The sunrise factor does not remove the regulation 64D request, delay, and return considerations. fca_statement_treated_as_waiver is false.

unverified.statement: No number of days was found for 'a reasonable time' in regulation 64D(2)(c)(ii), regulation 64E(2)(b)(ii), or the JMLSG paragraphs opened.
The JMLSG ministerial-approval page states that approval was received. It did not show a date when opened on 26 October 2026.
The revisions page did not list an Annex I later than August 2023. That does not prove no other version exists. Paragraphs 13 and 45 of the PDF that was opened still say 1,000 euros.
The FCA statement does not say that a sunrise receipt waives regulation 64D. This starter does not treat it as a waiver. Whether a court or the FCA would read it that way was not decided.
Regulation 14A, which defines a cryptoasset exchange provider and a custodian wallet provider, was not opened. The checklist uses the Part 7A cross-reference and does not restate the definition.

The sanctions regime and the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 were not opened. A firm marker is passed through as a reason to escalate. It is not a legal analysis, and it is not a suspicious activity report.
Regulation 64B defines a working day using bank holidays in any part of the United Kingdom. That calendar is not encoded, so no due date is returned for regulation 64C(2).

The Copilot Studio harness overview was opened on 26 October 2026. The separate billing and standard-harness licensing articles were not re-opened that day. Licence coverage beyond the overview is unverified.
